issue: Does Honeycutt v. United States's limit on forfeiture to property the defendant actually acquired apply to forfeiture under 18 U.S.C. § 981(a)(1)(C)?

sides.position: Honeycutt applies to forfeiture under 18 U.S.C. § 981(a)(1)(C), so a defendant may be ordered to forfeit only tainted property he actually acquired, not a co-conspirator's share.
cases: United States v. Elias, No. 23-6626 (2d Cir. 2025)

sides.position: Forfeiture under 18 U.S.C. § 981(a)(1)(C) is not limited by Honeycutt to property the defendant actually acquired, so a defendant may be held liable for proceeds obtained by co-participants.

this_court: Honeycutt applies to 18 U.S.C. § 981(a)(1)(C), and Elias was ordered to forfeit property he never acquired, so the forfeiture order is vacated.
quote: In so concluding, we join the Third, Ninth, and Eleventh Circuits on one side of a growing circuit split on the question, reaching a conclusion at odds with that of the Sixth and Eighth Circuits.
cite: United States v. Elias, No. 23-6626 (2d Cir. 2025)
